The bug was a logic inversion in SpacesAroundOperatorsFilter._process in sqlparse/filters/others.py. The condition for inserting a trailing space after an operator was `if not (next_ and next_.ttype != T.Whitespace):` which is equivalent to `if next_ is None or next_.ttype == T.Whitespace:` — i.e. it inserted a space only when there was already whitespace (or no next token), and skipped insertion when a non-whitespace token immediately followed the operator (the actual case needing a space). I fixed it to `if next_ and next_.ttype != T.Whitespace:`, which correctly inserts a space only when the next token exists and is not already whitespace. Verified with manual checks: '1+1' -> '1 + 1', 'foo(1+2)' -> 'foo(1 + 2)', 'a AND b<1' -> 'a AND b < 1', 'a=1 and b=2' -> 'a = 1 and b = 2', all now correctly spaced on both sides of the operator.
